html:
Belize is a small country on the Caribbean coast of Central America, between Mexico and Guatemala. For most of the time shown on the map it was a British settlement and then the colony of British Honduras.

Long before, it was Maya country. Cities such as Caracol and Lamanai were part of the world of the Maya city-states, which flourished here until about 1200.

English and Scottish woodcutters, the Baymen, settled the coast in the 1600s. They cut logwood for dye and later mahogany, using enslaved Africans brought through the Atlantic slave trade. Spain claimed the land and attacked the settlers several times, but failed at the Battle of St. George's Caye in 1798. In 1802 the first Garifuna, people of mixed African and Carib descent, began arriving from Honduras.

Britain made the settlement the colony of British Honduras in 1862. It was renamed Belize in 1973 and became independent in 1981.

Guatemala long claimed all of Belize as its own, so British troops stayed on after independence. Guatemala recognised the new state in 1991, but the border dispute went to the International Court of Justice after both countries voted in referendums to send it there. English is the official language, and Spanish, Kriol, Garifuna and Maya languages are all spoken.
sum: Belize is a small country on the Caribbean coast of Central America, between Mexico and Guatemala. For most of the time shown on the map it was a British settlement and then the colony of British Honduras.
